title: Safety, Permission, and Professional Judgment
summary: Practice deciding what is safe and authorized before acting on infrastructure.
objectives: Recognize when a task is outside a learner's authority.
Choose safe escalation instead of improvising around a control.

vocab.def: Permission to perform a particular task in a particular environment.
Passing a question or issue to someone with the right responsibility.

sections.heading: Stop before you act
sections.body: A professional checks permission, safety, and scope before changing a system. A warning is not an invitation to open equipment or bypass a control.

sections.heading: Infrastructure examples
sections.body: Mains power, energized hardware, live fiber, production credentials, and industrial cooling belong to qualified or explicitly supervised environments. In a classroom simulation, record the observation and escalate.

practice.prompt: A simulated rack has a temperature warning and an unfamiliar access control. What is the safe next step?
practice.answer: Record the evidence and ask the authorized instructor or facilities team.

quiz.question: What should happen before a learner changes a system?

lab.objective: Classify infrastructure actions by permission and safety boundary.

reflectionPrompt: When is not acting the most professional technical decision?

careerConnection.text: Technicians protect people and systems by following scope, permissions, and escalation procedures. This lesson is preparation, not qualification.
